sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
hindiTranslation: काम, क्रोध और लोभ  ये तीन प्रकारके नरकके दरवाजे जीवात्माका पतन करनेवाले हैं, इसलिये इन तीनोंका त्याग कर देना चाहिये ॥
englishTranslation: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates of ruin. Abandon these three.
essence: Three inner forces open the way to ruin; dropping them protects the self.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Desire, anger, and greed are the three forces that drag a person downward. Krishna says they must be given up.
simpleInsight: You do not have to obey every impulse. Freedom begins when you stop feeding the forces that trap you.
detailedMeaning: Krishna now names the inner enemies that make clear action impossible: desire, anger, and greed. He says these must be dropped before a person can act rightly.
modernRelevance: Before signing a loan for a flat beyond your means, ask which gate you are walking through: desire, anger at a sibling who bought first, or greed. Krishna says to leave all three.
translationLiteral: त्रिविधम् (threefold) / नरकस्य (of ruin) / इदम् (this) / द्वारम् (gate) / नाशनम् (destroyer) / आत्मनः (of the self) / कामः (desire) / क्रोधः (anger) / तथा (and also) / लोभः (greed) / तस्मात् (therefore) / एतत् (these) / त्रयम् (three) / त्यजेत् (should abandon)
insight: Krishna names three gates of ruin, desire, anger and greed, and tells Arjuna to abandon all three.

quoteVariants.text: Desire, anger, and greed ruin you. Leave them behind.
These three are the real gates of ruin.
